findings.title: Faithful, well-structured port with strong behavioral test coverage
findings.description: The pure validator is a faithful, deliberately-more-lenient port of the guide's bash script (verified line-by-line against `project-documents/ai-project-guide/scripts/validate-slice-design`), the node file layer preflights all inputs before any result is emitted (so a caller never sees partial results alongside an error), and the CLI wires the documented exit-code contract (0/1/2) through the shared `handleError`/`setJsonMode` path. The three test files cover the real template, real passing designs, per-heading failure, the JSON contract, all exit-2 paths with empty stdout, and worktree-aware template resolution. No correctness, typing, or testing-standard violations found.

findings.title: `slice-design` docType string exists in two places (pre-existing convention, not a defect of this change)
findings.description: `SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE = 'slice-design'` is introduced here, while `frontmatterSchema.ts` already hard-codes the same string in the `values: ['slice-design']` constraint for the `slice-design` docType. This is the existing project convention (the schema's `values` array is "allowed values," a different context than the identity constant), so referencing the new constant from the schema is not feasible without changing schema semantics, and the current code is consistent. Noted only so a future consolidation is aware the literal is duplicated across the two modules.
